title: Entrance banner family

location.series: Pentagram / Natural History Museum case study

slide_intent: Use repetition to connect separate signs, because people approach a building from changing distances and angles.
strategic_value: Alternating dark and acid-yellow banners can make the Museum’s identity visible while connecting its name to active language.
demonstration: Three hanging banners pair a central dark identity panel with yellow panels carrying circular and repeated words.
practical_value: Compare a name-bearing banner with adjacent expressive panels before distributing functions across a signage set.

content_islands.name: Central identifier
content_islands.spec: Place the museum name and circular symbol on the dark central banner.

content_islands.name: Flanking word patterns
content_islands.spec: Use yellow panels with repeated words and circular arrangements on both sides.

content_islands.name: Setting
content_islands.spec: Retain the building and trees behind the suspended group.

reference_purposes.Application: Three hanging banners pair a central dark identity panel with yellow panels carrying circular and repeated words.
